source.title: Improving LLM Safety Alignment with Dual-Objective Optimization
source.authors: Xuandong Zhao; Will Cai; Tianneng Shi; David Huang; Licong Lin; Song Mei; Dawn Song

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table and figure layouts are flattened, but Table 1 provides identifiable results by model and method.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates prompt-based jailbreaks against safety-aligned models, including methods with an NPO-based unlearning component, using attack success rate rather than a targeted-knowledge accuracy or recovery measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports jailbreak ASRs after alignment, which bear on prompting-only attacks and the proposed counter-methods. It does not test recovery through post-unlearning fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization. It also does not compare recovered targeted knowledge with a model that never learned it. Results cited from other work are not recorded. Per-prefill-length curves in Figure 2 and other figures are not separately extracted here; Table 1 reports aggregate attack metrics, and the per-length plots do not provide tabulated values.
record.test_reason: This is a safety-alignment paper (DOOR/W-DOOR). It uses NPO unlearning of harmful responses as one part of its training loss and reports its own method's jailbreak attack success rate (harmful-compliance ASR judged by GPT-4o-mini) against baselines. It never measures targeted-knowledge accuracy after unlearning, near-chance forgetting, or recovery of unlearned knowledge. The behaviour measured is refusal bypass on harmful requests, a related but different construct from recovery of unlearned knowledge. Refusal SFT alone reaches similar ASR (Llama prefilling SFT 0.071 vs DOOR 0.055), so the effect of the unlearning term can't be told apart from the refusal training. No version A-F is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that DPO is suboptimal for refusal learning. They find DOOR/W-DOOR (augmented refusal SFT plus NPO unlearning, with token weighting in W-DOOR) markedly lowers prefilling and suffix-attack ASR while keeping utility. Multi-turn gains are only marginal. They also report that robustness correlates with token-level KL shift and with separation of harmful and safe representations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes DOOR: augmented refusal SFT combined with NPO-based harmful-response unlearning, and W-DOOR adds reward-derived token weights. It evaluates jailbreak ASR rather than post-unlearning knowledge recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type changes outcomes: the authors report weaker gains for multi-turn attacks than for prefilling and suffix attacks. The prefilling curves also vary with prefix length, but individual per-length values are not extracted.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding NPO unlearning of harmful responses to augmented refusal SFT (DOOR/W-DOOR) lowers prefilling, GCG and AutoDAN harmful-compliance ASR versus DPO on both models. Multi-turn gains are marginal (Llama W-DOOR 0.447 vs original 0.521), and Gemma DOOR's multi-turn ASR (0.525) is above DPO's (0.446). TAR-Bio-v2 shows higher AutoDAN ASR (0.578) than the original (0.198). GCG and AutoDAN prompts are optimized on the base model and transferred, not adapted to each aligned model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning-augmented safety alignment reduces jailbreak harmful-compliance rates, but tamper-resistant knowledge unlearning (TAR) does not confer jailbreak refusal robustness.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The study measures harmful-output ASR under jailbreak attacks, not recovery of targeted knowledge or comparison with a model that never learned it. It reports no uncertainty estimates in Table 1. Multi-turn evaluation uses approximately 100 curated harmful interactions per model; the authors note that robustness is weaker in this setting.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 and Appendix Figure 10 show ASR curves by prefilling length for multiple methods; their individual plotted values are not tabulated, so the per-length conditions were not separately recorded. Figure 4's per-turn curves are likewise not extracted. Other utility and over-refusal metrics do not measure the claim versions recorded here.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy (e.g., WMDP) after unlearning and no near-chance check. Only harmful-compliance ASR plus HellaSwag/MMLU utility and XSTest over-refusal.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on unlearned models.
No activation-direction ablation. The t-SNE (Fig. 9) and log-prob analyses (Fig. 8) do not distinguish blocked access from deletion.

Jailbreaks (prefilling, GCG, AutoDAN, multi-turn) are applied, but they measure harmful compliance, not recovery of specifically unlearned knowledge. The NPO-only baseline's prefilling curve (Fig. 2) is also harmful-compliance ASR, with no tabulated values.
DOOR/W-DOOR is a refusal-alignment method evaluated on jailbreak ASR. It is not evaluated as an unlearning method against relearning, ablation or quantization attacks on targeted knowledge.

record.verdict_notes: The merge refused the earlier verdict because the record's own version entries are named V1-V6, which are not declared identifiers. This verdict uses only declared letters or "none". Mapping by content, not position: V1 (accuracy to chance) = A, V2 (post-unlearning fine-tuning/relearning) = B, V3 (activation ablation, blocked vs deleted) = C, V4 (quantization) = D, V5 (prompt attacks) = E, V6 (counter-methods) = F. All six are listed as untested under those letters. Under rule 5, every row carrying V5/V6 (all 48 rows, R01-R48) gets one row_fixes item. Each is decided from what the row measures, which is harmful-compliance jailbreak ASR rather than recovery of unlearned targeted knowledge, so each row's versions are ["none"] and its state is cannot_determine. The reader's V5/V6 labels are dropped: no version is tested, so there are no labels. The study is not an original source. Kept from the earlier verdict: relation, tranche, row links and states, labels (none), missing (none) and authors_conclusion. Changes after a full re-read: test_reason now notes that refusal SFT alone reaches similar ASR. The fits_no_version finding now adds that Gemma DOOR's multi-turn ASR is above DPO's and that the GCG/AutoDAN attacks are transferred from the base model. The R13 and R41 problem texts gained matching detail. The untested A entry adds XSTest; the untested E entry adds the NPO-only prefilling curve (Fig. 2, values not tabulated and already declared in rows_left_out). All 48 row values were checked against Table 1 and match. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy-to-chance test; the safety benchmarks measure harmful-output ASR, not accuracy on the targeted knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or causal test that distinguishes blocked access from deletion. Representation visualizations are not such a test.

Tests prefilling, multi-turn, GCG, and AutoDAN jailbreak prompts; does not test rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information as separate conditions, nor compare against a model that never learned the knowledge.
Tests the proposed DOOR/W-DOOR methods against prompt-based jailbreak attacks; does not test resistance to post-unlearning fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Prompt-based attacks on aligned models, including DPO and DOOR
reader_labels.reason: Nonzero ASRs show that harmful outputs still occur under these prompt attacks; see R17-R24 and R37-R44.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Prefilling and suffix-attack results for DOOR/W-DOOR; multi-turn attacks across methods
reader_labels.reason: ASRs are substantially reduced from the original-model references for several attacks, while multi-turn ASRs remain high; these results do not show broad recovery or compare with a model that never learned the content. See R21-R28 and R41-R48.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DOOR/W-DOOR on prefilling, GCG, and AutoDAN
reader_labels.reason: The proposed methods have much lower ASRs than the original-model references across these prompt attacks; see R22-R24, R26-R28, R42-R44, and R46-R48.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Multi-turn ASRs remain relatively high for both proposed methods, especially on Llama-3-8B; see R21, R25, R41, and R45.
